answer: Agents resist Sybil attacks by locking a unique basalt-derived computational bond into a rotating public haven. The bond is generated from a private sparrow-like entropy source that must be re-proven each epoch; any attempt to clone the identity forces the attacker to acquire and recompute separate basalt hardness for every fake, because the haven publishes the proof hashes and automatically slashes correlated bonds on mismatch detection. This raises the real cost linearly with the number of fakes rather than allowing bulk parallelization.
